newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh seeks bids for oil blocks.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh seeks bids for oil blocks.

text.p: Bangladesh expects to attract more than $500 million in annual investment as the world's top oil companies participate in July 15 bidding for 15 oil and gas blocks in the country, energy ministry officials said on Monday.
"We expect the world's 20 major companies to participate in the bidding. Huge foreign funds will be flowing into the country from next year," Energy Secretary Tawfiq-e-Elahi Chowdhury told Reuters.

The officials said the major companies expected to participate in the bidding include U.S. companies Exxon Corp, Mobil Corp Texaco Corp, Enron Corp., Unocal Corp and Chevron Corp., Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Tullow Oil Plc of Ireland.

They said some of the companies were likely to tie up to jointly explore for gas in Bangladesh. Production sharing contracts with the successful bidders will be completed by December this year, they said.
Chowdhury said he was hopeful of deals on most of the blocks. "We expect more than $500 million (of) investment by the companies annually from next year," he said.

The officials said the government had already appointed U.S. company Arthur Andersen to assist state-owned oil and gas company Petrobangla evaluate the bids, negotiate with the selected bidders and finalise the contracts.
Chowdhury said foreign experts believed "Bangladesh is floating on gas. The country has surplus gas compared to its long term demand."
Some experts saw Bangladesh as a hub in a potential transcontinental pipeline network, he said. He said Bangladesh could enter inter-regional cooperation in gas transmission.
The officials said India was showing interest in importing gas for its eastern states through a pipeline from Bangladesh's western region.
They said India even wanted to swap the gas from its northeastern Agartala field, which has reserves of about two trillion cubic feet.
Bangladesh has already offered eight blocks, two off-shore, to foreign companies which included British Cairn Energy Plc, Occidental Corp and United Meridian.
These companies are investing more than $800 million for exploration of gas and oil, the officials said.
The officials said the oil companies were particularly interested after Cairn's success in striking huge reserves in the Bay of Bengal.
The approximate gas reserve in the Sangu field, which Cairn Energy discovered last year, was about one trillion cubic feet. Cairn was investing $188 million in the two offshore blocks.
The officials said Bangladesh would buy 160 million cubic feet of gas per day from Cairn and 100 million cubic feet per day from Occidental from April next year under contracts signed recently.
Bangladesh offers duty free imports of machinery, allows repatriation of profits, and exemption of administration fees and corporate tax. It also has a clear-cut policy on gas pricing, they said.
Foreign companies will produce the gas at their own cost but they will be allowed to recover the cost first under the production-sharing contract.
The Petrobangla officials expected no negative impact on the foreign companies seeking investment because of last month's explosion at a gas field being developed by Occidental.
The officials said Bangladesh had now proven gas reserves of more than 10 trillion cubic feet. "But there are still huge gas reserves still undiscovered," said one official.
